correctness.rationale: For coordinate-exchangeable signs, pair correlation ρ=(E S²−n)/(n(n−1)) is bounded below by −1/(n−1) in even n and −1/n in odd n, with equality for the corresponding minimum-imbalance sign layers. Directly, E[z_i(Az)_i]=(1−ρ)A_ii+ρ(A1)_i gives the uniquely universally unbiased affine row-sum correction. For row i, variance of the corrected single probe equals (sum_{j≠i}A_ij²+ρ(sum_{j≠i}A_ij)^2)/(1−ρ). Independent probes divide variance by m, yielding total risk (||B||_F²+ρ||B1||²)/(m(1−ρ)). The derivative with respect to ρ is (||B||_F²+||B1||²)/(m(1−ρ)^2)>0 for nondiagonal A, hence minimum correlation is globally optimal in stated class. Cauchy–Schwarz gives even zero-risk rows precisely row-constant off diagonal; odd risk zero only B=0. Comparing with m+1 iid signs gives strict universal advantage for even n≥4 m≥n, odd n≥3 m≥n+1 and n=2 any m; B1=0 witnesses make boundaries exact. Independently enumerated all optimal fixed-count sign vectors for n=2..7 with rational matrix entries, checking unbiasedness and row variance; the dimension-general proof is algebraic.

value.rationale: The diagonal of a matrix accessed only by matrix–vector products is a natural computational invariant. Exact dimension/parity-sensitive risk and zero-error subspaces supply actionable sampling and budget decisions beyond generic concentration bounds. A deterministic row-sum query plus fixed-sum signs can exactly recover a dense row-constant-off-diagonal matrix for even dimensions; matched-budget crossover is sharp. Its restricted-class optimality is clear and mathematically motivated, not a claim of arbitrary estimator minimax.

limitations: Restriction to coordinate-permutation exchangeable signs with independent probes, exact A1, and a universally unbiased affine correction; no claim against all probing algorithms. Full XDiag text not inspected and source comparison remains best of knowledge.
